title: A Noetherian domain satisfies the Ore condition
notes: \ru{Всякое нёт. кольцо (без дел. 0) --- кольцо Оре}; the displayed condition is \(a,b\ne0\Rightarrow \exists x,y\ne0:xa=yb\).
statement: If \(R\) is an associative unital left-Noetherian domain, then \(Ra\cap Rb\ne0\) for every \(a,b\in R\setminus\{0\}\): \(R\) satisfies the left Ore condition. The right-sided assertion requires right Noetherianity. Enveloping algebras of finite-dimensional Lie algebras over a characteristic-zero field have both properties by the PBW filtration.
reconstruction: The side of Noetherianity and the unit convention are supplied. PBW is contextual explanation, not an extra assertion attributed to this page.
fate: Background ring theory, reproduced as Lemma 2 of \citet[\S1]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}; Ore localization predates the seminar \citep{ore1931linear}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The stated result is established with the hypotheses supplied here.

statement:
After the chain stabilizes, choose the least \(j\) with \(x_j

e0.\] If \(j=n\), the parenthesis is simply \(a\). This produces a nonzero common left multiple without assuming \(x_0

title: The Ore division ring of fractions
notes: \ru{Кольцо Оре вклад. в тело}; elements are written \(ab^{-1}\), described as equivalence classes.
statement: A unital domain satisfying the right Ore condition admits a division ring \(Q(R)\) in which every element is \(ab^{-1}\), \(a,b\in R\), \(b\ne0\). It is unique up to the isomorphism fixing \(R\). Left Ore gives the analogous construction with \(b^{-1}a\); a two-sided Ore domain has both descriptions.
reconstruction: The preceding displayed condition is left-sided, whereas the written fractions are right-sided. Both sides hold for the Noetherian rings subsequently used; a one-sided hypothesis alone should not silently be swapped.
fate: This is Ore\textquotesingle s fraction construction \citep{ore1931linear}, reviewed in \citet[\S1]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The stated result is established with the hypotheses supplied here.

title: The unresolved Green-operator remark
notes: An underlined line reads \ru{Дифф. опер. от [зачёркнуто] Грина[?], это тело!!}, followed by \ru{(и наоборот)}.
statement: No definite theorem is recoverable: a differential-operator ring itself is generally not a division ring, whereas adjoining formal inverses in an Ore localization is. The uncertain word may refer to Green operators, but no domain, boundary conditions or inverse convention is specified.
reconstruction: The two possible readings are kept apart. No analytic inverse, Green kernel or claim that every differential operator is invertible is supplied.
fate: The algebraic context is \citet{gelfandkirillov1966corps}; no exact publication match for this damaged sentence was identified.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The fragment remains underdetermined; it is not evidence for an undeveloped mathematical problem.

title: Weyl algebras with central parameters and their fraction fields
notes: \(R_{n,k}\) is the ring of differential operators in \(n\) variables with \(k\) commuting parameters; \(D_{n,k}\) is its division ring of ratios.
statement: Over a fixed characteristic-zero field \(L\), let \(R_{n,k}=A_n(L)\otimes_L L[z_1,\ldots,z_k]\), where \([p_i,q_j]=\delta_{ij}\), \([p_i,p_j]=[q_i,q_j]=0\), and all \(z_\ell\) are central. Set \(D_{n,k}=Q(R_{n,k})\). Here \(n,k\ge0\); \(D_{0,k}=L(z_1,\ldots,z_k)\).
reconstruction: The coefficient field, characteristic, commutator sign and meaning of independent central parameters are made explicit. Polynomial coefficients, rather than arbitrary smooth coefficients, are essential.
fate: Classical differential-operator and Ore constructions; this notation is formalized in \citet[\S\S2--3]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The stated result is established with the hypotheses supplied here.

title: Different Weyl ranks and parameter counts give nonisomorphic division rings
notes: For \(D_{n,k}\), \ru{При разных n и k неизом.}
statement: For a fixed characteristic-zero field \(L\), an \(L\)-algebra isomorphism \(D_{n,k}\simeq D_{n^{\prime},k^{\prime}}\) exists if and only if \((n,k)=(n^{\prime},k^{\prime})\). The same distinction holds for the rings \(R_{n,k}\). The division-ring statement needs the fraction-field invariant, not only the growth dimension of the polynomial subring.
reconstruction: Isomorphisms are required to fix \(L\). This extends the earlier Weyl-rank item 1964-38.1; it is not the endomorphism conjecture for a fixed Weyl algebra.
fate: Exactly the nonisomorphism theorem of \citet[\S4]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}; also announced by \citet{gelfandkirillov1966fields}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The stated result is established with the hypotheses supplied here.

title: Commutative leading symbols
notes: For an operator \(a\), \([a]\) denotes its leading part; \ru{В старш. ч. p и q коммут.}, and \([ab]=[a][b]\).
statement: Give each Weyl generator degree one and each central parameter degree one (or give the parameters degree zero over their coefficient ring). Then \(\operatorname{gr}R_{n,k}\) is the corresponding commutative polynomial domain. For nonzero \(a,b\), degree is additive and \(\sigma(ab)=\sigma(a)\sigma(b)\). The principal-symbol map is multiplicative on nonzero elements, not an additive map from the filtered ring to its graded ring.
reconstruction: The filtration must be specified. Its two natural versions are distinguished; no characteristic-zero operator ring is identified with its commutative associated graded ring.
fate: The standard filtered-operator argument is used explicitly in \citet[\S3]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The stated result is established with the hypotheses supplied here.

title: A well-defined multiplicative symbol of an Ore fraction
notes: For \(b=a_1a_2^{-1}\), the notes take \([a_1]/[a_2]\) and say that it depends only on \(b\), not its representation. The short continuation at the right edge is uncertain.
statement: The multiplicative symbol extends to \(D_{n,k}^{\times}\) by \(\sigma(a_1a_2^{-1})=\sigma(a_1)/\sigma(a_2)\). This is independent of the right-fraction expression, takes values in the multiplicative group of nonzero homogeneous rational functions of the chosen graded variables, and is invariant under inner automorphisms. It is not a division-ring homomorphism.
reconstruction: Inner invariance is the publication\textquotesingle s corollary, not a confident decipherment of the damaged right-edge fragment. Multiplicativity follows by taking common Ore denominators; commutativity of graded symbols removes conjugation.
fate: The independence statement and inner-invariance corollary are Lemma 4 of \citet[\S3]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The stated result is established with the hypotheses supplied here.

title: A universal determinant over a division ring
notes: \ru{Универс. det --- отобр. в фактор по коммутанту. То же в теле, универс. --- ?}
statement: For a division ring \(D\), what is the abelianization of the stable general linear group? The answer is \[K_1(D)=\mathrm{GL}_{\infty}(D)_{\mathrm{ab}}\simeq D^{\times}/[D^{\times},D^{\times}].\] The Dieudonn\'e determinant realizes this quotient; every group homomorphism from the stable general linear group to an abelian group factors uniquely through it. In characteristic zero this also holds in each finite matrix size at least two.
reconstruction: The notes do not specify matrix size. The stable formulation removes the small finite-field exception \(\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_2)\); the Weyl fields here have characteristic zero.
fate: The division-ring determinant and its universal abelian quotient were established by \citet[\S\S5--7]{dieudonne1943determinants}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: This is the established Dieudonn\'e determinant, not a remaining open determinant problem.

title: Determine all automorphisms of the Weyl division ring
notes: \ru{Найти все автоморфизмы этого тела (тр. зад.)}; below it: \ru{(Пр. Фурье + умн. на ф-ю)}.
statement: For the previously defined \(D_{n,k}\), determine its automorphisms over the coefficient field. A precise minimal case is \(\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb C}D_{1,0}\), where \(D_{1,0}=Q(\mathbb C\langle x,p\mid px-xp=1\rangle)\). The question concerns the division ring, not just automorphisms or endomorphisms of its polynomial Weyl subalgebra.
reconstruction: The base field and the case \(n=1,k=0\) are explicit restrictions for development. Nothing on the page asserts that Fourier transforms and multiplication operators generate every automorphism. No novel general solution is claimed below.
fate: Polynomial automorphisms are understood \citep{makarlimanov1984automorphisms}; rational subfield stabilizers are classified by \citet[Proposition 2.2]{alevdumas1998invariants}. These are partial answers to the notebook\textquotesingle s unrestricted question.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The full group is not classified in the verified literature: \citet[\S5.3.3]{dumas2011invariants} states the gap; searches through this date found no later full classification. \citet[Theorem 0.12]{schwarz2024generalizations} concerns induced finite-group invariant fields, not all division-ring automorphisms. The development proves a restricted classification and an exact rational-pole criterion; the unrestricted problem is left open. The November 2026 index-symmetry theorem of \citet[Corollary 8.12]{lauritzenthomsen2026duality} is a further related result, not an automorphism classification.
worth: Worth a bounded development of rational subfield stabilizers and inner-conjugation obstructions, because these answer a precise part of the handwritten question without presuming a classification of the full group.

title: Fourier transforms and multiplication as automorphism constructions
notes: The parenthesis to the automorphism problem suggests Fourier transform plus multiplication by a function.
statement: For \(D_{1,0}\) with \([p,x]=1\), the algebraic Fourier map \(x\mapsto p\), \(p\mapsto-x\) is an automorphism. For \(u\in\mathbb C(x)^{\times}\), conjugation by multiplication by \(u\) gives \(x\mapsto x\), \(p\mapsto p-u^{\prime}/u\). Multiplication alone is not a unital algebra automorphism. More generally every rational shift \(p\mapsto p+h(x)\) is an automorphism, but need not be inner.
reconstruction: The notebook\textquotesingle s operation on functions is interpreted as conjugation on the operator algebra; invertibility of \(u\) and the rational coefficient restriction are supplied. The last distinction is proved in the development.
fate: Fourier transformations already motivate \citet{gelfandkirillov1966corps}; the rational stabilizer context is made precise in \citet{alevdumas1998invariants}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The stated result is established with the hypotheses supplied here.

title: Growth dimension and the missing logarithm
notes: For generators \(\alpha=(a_1,\ldots,a_s)\), the displayed numerator is \(d(\alpha,N)\), described as the number of linearly independent monomials of degree at most \(N\); the denominator is \(\ln N\).
statement: The correct algebra growth invariant is \[\operatorname{GKdim}_L A=\sup_V\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log\dim_L V^N}{\log N},\] where \(V\) runs over finite-dimensional \(L\)-subspaces containing \(1\), and \(V^N\) is the span of products of at most \(N\) factors. For finitely generated \(A\), any finite-dimensional generating \(V\ni1\) suffices. Without the numerator logarithm, even \(L[x]\) has an infinite displayed value.
reconstruction: The normalized logarithmic growth is a mathematical emendation, not a new reading of the ink. Independence of generators follows from \(V\subseteq W^c\) and \(W\subseteq V^d\). For quotient division rings the 1966 paper uses a different invariant with a denominator-clearing infimum; replacing that invariant by naive algebra growth is unjustified.
fate: The logarithm is present in formula (6) of \citet[\S4]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}; the scan confirms its omission in the notebook.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The corrected invariant is Gelfand--Kirillov dimension. The handwritten omission is substantive and is recorded in the correction apparatus.

title: Growth dimension of the parameterized Weyl algebra
statement: For \(R_{n,k}=A_n(L)\otimes L[z_1,\ldots,z_k]\) with the total-degree generating filtration and \(\operatorname{char}L=0\), ordered PBW monomials form a basis and \[\dim_L F_N R_{n,k}=\binom{N+2n+k}{2n+k}.\] Consequently \(\operatorname{GKdim}_L R_{n,k}=2n+k\), including the scalar case \(n=k=0\).
reconstruction: This conclusion uses the corrected logarithmic definition. The ordered-monomial count includes the identity and central parameters and is not asserted to count all noncommuting words separately. \oursComputed\ The independent finite checks, including \(n=k=0\) and \(N=0\), are saved in \texttt{code/check\_weyl.py} and its two output files.
fate: This is Lemma 5 of \citet[\S4]{gelfandkirillov1966corps}; the count is checked independently in the supplied computation.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The stated result is established with the hypotheses supplied here.
